facts.label: CMD Brijendra Pratap Singh appointment and background
facts.value: Brijendra Pratap Singh selected by PESB (17-Sep-2024) as NALCO CMD; assumed charge 8-Jan-2025 at Bhubaneswar, succeeding Sridhar Patra (retired 31-Oct-2024). Mining Machinery Engineering graduate, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad 1989; MBA Marketing. 35+ years in SAIL — career at Bhilai, Bokaro, Durgapur, IISCO steel plants; immediately prior was Director-in-Charge, Burnpur & Durgapur Steel Plant and SAIL board member.

facts.label: Director (Finance) Abhay Kumar Behuria appointment and background
facts.value: Abhay Kumar Behuria assumed charge as Director (Finance), NALCO on 11-Jun-2025 (Ministry of Mines order dated 6-Jun-2025). B.Com (Hons.) First Class, Utkal University; Fellow Member ICAI (Institute of Cost Accountants of India); Executive Diploma in Business Valuation (ICMAI). Prior role: Executive Director (Finance & Accounts), Rourkela Steel Plant (SAIL) — credited with record EBITDA/PBT at RSP, unit closures/cost optimization, SAP-in-Mines and digital finance initiatives.

facts.label: Other whole-time/functional directors on NALCO board
facts.value: Director (Commercial): Anil Kumar Singh, effective 7-Jan-2026, 35+ yrs commercial/metals experience, prior GM (Materials & Contracts) and I/c-HR at Hindustan Copper, career started at RINL. Director (Production): Pankaj Kumar Sharma, assumed charge 1-Feb-2023, 30+ yrs open-cast mining, career at NMDC. Director (Personnel/HR) not identified in this search pass — flagged as gap.

facts.label: Cessation of three Independent Directors effective 31-Mar-2026
facts.value: Ms. Trupti Kamlesh Patel, Dr. Ajay Narang and Shri Patel Sanjaykumar ceased to be Independent Directors effective 31-Mar-2026 on natural tenure expiry (Reg. 30 LODR disclosure). NALCO noted, per its CPSE structure, that Independent Director appointments are vested with the President of India and outside company control — implying a board-composition/independent-oversight gap risk until GoI appoints replacements.

facts.value: No SEBI enforcement order, show-cause notice, ED/SFIO/CBI action, or NCLT/NCLAT/IBBI petition against NALCO or its directors was found in this search pass (searches covered SEBI orders, NCLT filings, SFIO/CBI/ED mentions). facts.label: Panchpatmali bauxite mining lease renewal dates — correction vs. management-stated 2029/2035
facts.value: Per Odisha Government mining-lease extension orders as recorded in the Indian Bureau of Mines Bauxite Yearbook (2019 edition, covering extensions from 31-Mar-2020 base): Panchpatmali North-Central Block lease extended to 16-Nov-2032; Panchpatmali South Block lease extended to 19-Jul-2029. This ANALYST QUESTION asked to verify mgmt-stated 'central block 2029, south 2035' — the primary-source-derived dates found (South Block 2029, North-Central 2032) do NOT match the mgmt framing quoted in the brief (which has central=2029, south=2035); the block-to-date pairing appears reversed and the terminal dates differ (2032 vs 2035 for the non-South block). This is flagged as a DISCREPANCY requiring verification against NALCO's own AR/investor-presentation disclosure of lease terms, which is the more current and authoritative source than this 2019-vintage IBM yearbook chapter.
facts.period: as of 2019-2020 extension; may have been further renewed since

facts.label: Pottangi bauxite mine — lease, contractor, and startup timeline
facts.value: Odisha Government granted NALCO a 50-year mining lease over ~697.979 hectares at Pottangi, Koraput district (lease deed signed/reported 14-Jun-2024); rated capacity 3.5 MTPA, reserves ~111 million tonnes, ~32-year mine life. Dilip Buildcon emerged as lowest bidder (L1) for mine development-cum-operation. As of Dec-2025 reporting, NALCO targeted start of mining by June 2026, alongside a Damanjodi refinery 5th stream (+1 MTPA, taking capacity from 2.275 to ~3.275 MTPA) and a parallel-conveyor contingency (~30 lakh tonnes/year capacity from existing mines) commissioning Apr-May 2026 as a hedge against Pottangi delay.

facts.label: Tribal/community opposition to Pottangi (Serubandha Hills) bauxite project — execution risk to the June-2026 startup target
facts.value: Sustained tribal opposition in Koraput district (Serubandha Hills / Serubandh Suraksha Samiti) to the Pottangi-linked bauxite mining project on grounds of displacement, forest loss and water-source (perennial stream) depletion. An August-2024 foundation ceremony (bhumi pujan), to be attended by the Union Minister of State for Mines, was stalled/called off after villagers demanded land-acquisition/settlement issues be resolved first. As of an April-2026 long-form report, unrest in the wider Eastern Ghats bauxite belt (including areas historically mined by NALCO at Panchpatmali) continues to be described as unresolved. This is an OPINION-INFLECTED reputational/execution-risk item from advocacy/NGO-adjacent sources (LandConflictWatch, Countercurrents) and should be read as one-sided community-advocacy framing, not adjudicated fact — but the underlying protest events (stalled bhumi pujan, demands re: land settlement) are corroborated across independent press (AlCircle, OrissaPOST).

facts.label: Utkal-D and Utkal-E captive coal block lease status
facts.value: Utkal-E: mining lease granted ~Apr-2021, 30-year term, 523.73 ha, Angul district, ~70 mt mineable reserve, initial capacity 2 MTPA. Utkal-D: 30-year lease secured approx. one month prior (~Mar-2021). Combined Utkal-D&E: mining lease deed for the amalgamated block reported signed 24-Dec-2024, 30-year term valid to 21-Apr-2051; combined mineable reserve ~175 million tonnes; feeds NALCO's captive power plant at the Angul Smelter & Power Complex (operational since Nov-2022); FY2025-26 target to lift coal production to 4 million tonnes.

facts.label: GoI disinvestment / OFS history and current signal for NALCO
facts.value: No OFS or strategic-disinvestment transaction for NALCO found in this search pass. Ministry of Mines (Minister Pralhad Joshi) stated in Rajya Sabha (21-Mar-2022) that no decision had been taken to disinvest NALCO, following political opposition (CPI's D. Raja letter to PM, Feb-2022) to reported privatisation plans. BALCO and Hindustan Zinc — the two Ministry-of-Mines CPSEs that WERE privatised — are cited by contrast as already-completed disinvestments; NALCO has not followed. A more recent (2026) trade-press item (AlCircle) reports NALCO management 'rules out divestment', citing confidence in the aluminium cycle — this is a management/company-level statement, not a government policy statement, and should be read as management's characterization. No FY2026 OFS calendar entry for NALCO found (the only 2026 Ministry-of-Mines-adjacent OFS activity found was NLC India's 3% OFS, June 2026 — a different company, included here only to confirm it is NOT NALCO).

facts.label: NALCO dividend payout pattern FY2025 and FY2026 (multiple interims), DIPAM-context
facts.value: NALCO paid Rs.988.88 crore in dividend to the Government of India for FY2024-25 (company press release). For FY2025-26, the company declared multiple interim dividends through the year (board meeting scheduled 30-Jan-2026 to consider a second interim; a subsequently reported 3rd interim dividend of Rs.2/share brought total FY26 dividend to Rs.10.50/share, alongside Q4 standalone net profit of Rs.1,718 cr). This pattern of multiple interim dividends across the fiscal year is consistent with DIPAM's general capital-efficiency push for CPSEs (minimum dividend norms of higher of 30% of PAT or 4-5% of net worth, per standing DIPAM guidelines) though this search pass did not locate a NALCO-specific DIPAM directive letter — the company's own Dividend Distribution Policy document (nalcoindia.com) was identified but not fetched in this pass (fetch budget prioritized elsewhere); flagged as gap for follow-up if dividend-policy specifics become load-bearing.
